title: Application-level gate: no submit_record without a successful validate_record
exam_question: What change would most effectively enforce the required workflow?
correct_option_text: Add an application-level gate that blocks submit_record unless validate_record has succeeded for the same record.
why: Claude only emits a tool_use request; the application executes it. That boundary is where business-critical ordering is enforced deterministically. Prompt wording and tool_choice steer behaviour but cannot prove a prerequisite was met; stopping the loop on phrases like 'ready to submit' is the anti-pattern the exam warns about.
rubric: Learner can point to the line in the gate that checks validated[record_id] before executing submit_record.
Learner explains why the gate returns is_error: true rather than silently dropping the call.
Learner states why tool_choice: tool for validate_record would not have been sufficient.
task: Run a manual agent loop (stop_reason == tool_use) over the four tools. The gate refuses submit_record for any record_id without a prior validate_record success and returns a tool_result with is_error: true, so Claude has to validate and, for the ambiguous document, open a review ticket instead.
prompt_template:
<document>
{{document}}
</document>
Extract this document's fields, validate the record, then submit it. Record id: {{record_id}}. If a required field is ambiguous, open a review ticket instead of guessing.
gate: submit_record executes only when validated[record_id] is True

response.error: blocked by application gate: validate_record has not succeeded for this record_id
response.required_next_step: call validate_record, or create_review_ticket if a required field is ambiguous
